text:
maria: FYI - ACME reported p99 spikes ~4s, and a bunch of 401s. They say requests that set region=eu-west-1 are landing in us-east-1. Escalating to oncall. ticket: #4521

sam: copying in jordan and kevin. can you paste a sample request id + headers?

maria: here's the header dump they sent:```
X-Request-ID: req_01FZ8ABCD
X-Region: eu-west-1
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_... (scoped to eu)
```
But response shows server-region header: `x-served-region: us-east-1` and body has `error: unauthorized`

jordan: looking at routing logs now. I see the request hitting our edge in eu-west-1, then being proxied to us-east-1. There is an entry in the route-cache for the model shard that points to us-east-1 with last_updated ~2h ago.

sam: were there any recent changes to routing config or a deploy?

jordan: we shipped a small perf patch last night that touched route-cache TTL handling. preliminary guess: TTL being set to 0 on some keys so fallback path used stale next-hop.

maria: customer is seeing retries and exponential backoff churn. They reported increased token usage (billing spike) while they retried.

kevin: can you capture the retry pattern / X-Idempotency-Key presence? If they retried without idempotency, duplicates will bill. We'll need to offer a credit if it's on our side.

maria: they weren't setting `Idempotency-Key`. logs show repeated attempts for same session id.

jordan: mitigation idea — purge route-cache for eu model cluster, and temporarily pin eu traffic to true eu pairs. I'll run a targeted purge.

sam: do it. also add a short fallback policy change: prefer same-region, do not cross-region unless all same-region endpoints unhealthy for > 30s.

jordan: running purge command: `redwoodctl routes purge --cluster models-eu --force`

deploy-bot: purge job started (job_id: purge_9032).

deploy-bot: purge job completed successfully. 124 keys removed.

jordan: routing table refreshed. asking ACME to re-test.

maria: ACME confirms latency back to normal and 401s gone. they still saw extra billing for the last hour.

kevin: prepare credit estimate. ask support to request their total tokens for window 10:20-11:10 UTC. I'll calc.

sam: follow-up actions: 1) revert/patch TTL bug — ensure non-zero default and add unit test 2) change fallback policy to respect region affinity threshold 3) add monitoring alert for cross-region routing spikes 4) customer credit + postmortem.

jordan: opened infra ticket INF-981 to patch TTL and add test. scheduling patch for today.

maria: I've attached the support ticket and customer repro steps to the incident. URL: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-981 (internal)

kevin: billing note added to INF-981. assigned to me for credit calc.

sam: thanks team. great coordination. once INF-981 merges, let's roll a canary and watch routing-mismatch alert. :thumbsup:

maria: closing this Slack thread; moved the rest to the incident doc and the support ticket. tagging follow-up owners above. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated. incident_id=inc_2026-03-05-4521

deploy-bot: canary for INF-981 deployed to eu region at 1827543600.

maria: final note for postmortem: root cause = route-cache TTL regression after perf patch, which allowed fallback logic to pick remote region; contributing factor = customers retrying without idempotency increased billing impact. remediation = patch TTL, tighten fallback, alerting, customer credit.

sam: assigning postmortem author to jordan. please include timeline, RCA, and follow-up verification steps.

jordan: will do. expected PM upload by EOD tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. closing.
